_readme: LIMITED-TIME EVENTS. 09-game-modes.md §14, 03-screens-and-navigation.md §4.4.3,
and 07-economy-and-monetization.md (event currencies, §8.4 reruns).
An event is a data bundle: run windows, a currency of its own, missions, a shop,
and the modes it points at. Adding an event needs no code — that is the point.
RUNS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT PROMISED. §14 makes reruns policy: 'every event returns
within 2 seasons' and 'nothing gameplay-relevant is permanently missable'. A
promise in prose is not a schedule, so every run window an event will ever have
is written here from the start — exactly as banners.json does it. checkEventData()
refuses an event with fewer than two runs, refuses runs that overlap, and refuses
a gap between consecutive runs longer than rerunWithinWeeks. That is what makes
'nothing is permanently missable' a property of the data rather than a hope.
HONEST TIMERS. Every window is a real UTC datetime and the screen prints the real
end. There is no countdown that outlives its event and no 'ends soon!' that means
nothing. An event that has ended reads as ended, with the date it returns.
EVENT CURRENCY NEVER EXPIRES INTO NOTHING. 07 §3: leftover tokens convert to Clout
at 1:5 when a run ends, logged in the inbox. conversionToClout is that 5, in one
place, so the screen's promise and the payout cannot drift apart.
MISSION OBJECTIVES ARE THE MISSIONS SYSTEM'S OWN. The 'objective' block below is
the same Objective type data/missions.json uses, measured by the same code. Event
missions are credited per match rather than recomputed from the outcome log,
because that log is pruned to what the daily and weekly rotation still needs —
roughly a week, against a fortnight-long event. Credit has to be additive to be
correct, so 'distinct' requirements are refused here and only here: counting
distinct factions needs the whole set at once, and a running total cannot know
whether today's faction was already seen. checkEventData() enforces it.

_note: WEEKLY RULE MODIFIERS - 09-game-modes.md section 12, 'Remix Queue'.
Section 12 says the modifiers are 'data-driven event configs (data/events.json)',
so they live here rather than in a file of their own.
A modifier is built out of three general mechanisms the engine already had, and
no new ones:
balance     - MatchConfig.balanceOverrides, whose own comment in types.ts
already reads 'balance overrides for boss battles / weekly
modifiers'. The engine anticipated this mode.
passive     - CardPatch.passive, 'appended to a leader's passive list - how an
artifact attaches to a player'. A Remix passive is appended to
BOTH leaders, which is the only difference between a global rule
and a Doomscroll artifact.
costCeiling - every card costing more than this costs exactly this, applied as
computed cardOverrides. One general mechanism; Budget Cuts is the
only modifier that currently uses it.
All ten of section 12.1's launch rotation are listed, because the table is
content and dropping the four that need engine work would quietly rewrite the
spec. A modifier carrying a 'deferred' string is not in the rotation and must
carry no rule fields - checkRemixData enforces both halves, so a deferral cannot
hide a half-built rule and a rule cannot ship unannounced.

modifiers.name: Main Character Energy
modifiers.text: The first Character you play each turn gains Spotlight and +1/+1.

passive.text: Main Character Energy - the first Character you play each turn gains Spotlight and +1/+1.

modifiers.name: Everything Is Content
modifiers.text: The first card you play each turn gains Viral.

passive.text: Everything Is Content - the first card you play each turn gains Viral.

modifiers.name: Speedrun Any%
modifiers.text: Turn timer is 35 seconds. Both players draw 2 cards at the start of their turn.

_note: Deferred. 'Banished until that player's next turn' is a timed banish, and
banish in this engine is permanent - scheduleDelayed could return it, but
there is no target selector for 'the highest-Attack character on each side',
only highestCost and lowestCost. Two missing pieces, both engine work.
modifiers.name: Touch Some Grass
modifiers.text: At the start of each player's turn, the highest-Attack character on each side is Banished until that player's next turn.
modifiers.deferred: needs a highest-Attack target selector and a timed banish; the DSL has highestCost/lowestCost and a permanent banish, so both halves are engine work rather than authoring

_note: Deferred. The engine tracks confluence use per turn as a boolean
(player.confluenceUsedThisTurn), so 'two per turn' is not a number that can
be overridden - it is a counter the engine does not keep.
modifiers.name: Crossover Episode
modifiers.text: You may activate two Confluences per turn (each pair still once).
modifiers.deferred: the engine records confluence use as a per-turn boolean rather than a count, so there is no number for balanceOverrides to bend - it needs a real counter first

modifiers.name: Budget Cuts
modifiers.text: Max Hype is capped at 7. Cards costing 8 or more cost 7.

modifiers.name: Echo Chamber
modifiers.text: The first Action you play each turn adds a copy costing (1) more to your hand.

passive.text: Echo Chamber - the first Action you play each turn adds a copy costing (1) more to your hand.

_note: Deferred. This is a new thing the player DOES, not a rule about what
happens - it needs an intent, a button, an AI that knows when to press it
and a replay decoding. Every other modifier here is a passive or a number.
modifiers.name: Feed Refresh
modifiers.text: Once per turn, you may discard your hand and draw that many cards.
modifiers.deferred: a new player action, not a passive rule: it needs its own intent, a HUD control, AI that knows when to use it and a replay path, none of which a data-driven modifier can add

modifiers.name: Down Bad
modifiers.text: Both players gain 1 Obsession at the start of their turn. Fixations cost 2 Obsession.

passive.text: Down Bad - gain 1 Obsession at the start of your turn.

_note: Deferred, and the honest reason is that half of it is not a match rule at
all. The Prism splash limit is enforced by validateDeck when a deck is
SAVED, long before a match config exists, so a per-match override would
change nothing about the decks people bring. 'Refract may choose any
Current' is a real match rule and is engine work.
modifiers.name: Prism Party
modifiers.text: The Prism splash limit is removed this week; Refract may choose any Current.
modifiers.deferred: the splash limit is a deck-building rule enforced at save time, not a match rule, so a match-scoped override would not change which decks players bring; and letting Refract choose any Current is engine work in the confluence path

_note: The convention event, and the one that is running as this build ships.
Con Badges are one of the four event currencies 07 names by example.
events.name: HYPECON
events.blurb: Three halls, one working escalator, and a queue for a signing that ended yesterday. Wear the badge anyway.
rules: Every match played anywhere in the game counts toward HYPECON missions — the convention does not care which hall you are in.
Con Badges are earned from event missions only. They are not dropped, sold, or purchasable.
Badges left over when the doors close convert to Clout at 1 : 5, and the receipt lands in your inbox.

_note: The concluded one. Its first run is in the past as this build ships, which is
what gives the archive a real entry rather than an empty rail — and its second
run is the rerun notice §4.4.3 asks the archive to carry.
events.name: The Encore Livestream
events.blurb: Twelve hours of a stage nobody left. The chat replayed itself twice and nobody noticed.
rules: A concluded event is replayable as a Rerun: the missions and the shop return exactly as you left them.
Glowsticks you already earned are still yours when it comes back — progress and stock carry across runs.
Rerun entries pay base rewards. Nothing here is gone forever.

_note: The upcoming one, so the 'coming up' rail is not empty either. Pixel Pumpkins
is 07's own example currency for exactly this event.
events.name: Glitchoween
events.blurb: The render farm caught something. It is fine. The skeletons are supposed to clip through the floor like that.
rules: Glitchoween runs alongside the Weekly Boss and The Doomscroll — every match in either counts.
Pixel Pumpkins are earned from event missions only.
Leftovers convert to Clout at 1 : 5 when the run ends, with a receipt in your inbox.
